text:
incident-bot: PAGER — high error rate and latency for inference endpoints in us-west-2a (az1a). Alert: 5xx spikes + TCP retransmits. Trigger: inference-api-prod route 'gpt-medium' > 5% 5xx over 2m.
Samir P: I'm on it, paging on-call. tagging @Maria G for az ownership.
Maria G: I’m on-call, looking at dashboards now. seeing latency tail and 502/503. rolling error budget alarm.
Jin W: I can reproduce from my laptop: curl to inference endpoint times out intermittently. NLB logs show target health check failing for multiple nodes in az1a.
Liam R: same from telemetry — increased SYN retransmits from instances in az1a, ENI-level packet drops. Also see a bunch of RSTs around 14:24:xx UTC.
Samir P: Can someone run `kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide` for az1a nodes? check if kube-proxy or host networking is flapping.
Jin W: Paste: ```
# kubectl snippet
NAME                       READY   STATUS    NODE             NOMINATED
inference-svc-abcde        1/1     Running   ip-10-1-3-45     
inference-svc-fghij        1/1     Running   ip-10-1-3-46     
```
But connectivity from host to NLB target port 8080 fails intermittently.
Maria G: I'm seeing host-level drops on those two instances, rx errors and queue buildup. Could be ENI saturation or host NIC driver issues. AWS console shows increased ENI error counters for that AZ.
ops-bot: aws: Detected increased ENI packet drops in us-west-2a — creating incident ticket #INC-2026-1991.
Samir P: Immediate mitigations: 1) shift routing away from az1a to other AZs, 2) disable cross-AZ stickiness for this target group so clients reconnect to healthy targets, 3) scale up capacity in other AZs. Who can update routing policies?
Liam R: I can change NLB target group registration to set drained=on for the two bad instances, and adjust ALB weights. Doing that now.
Jin W: Before you drain, we should enable prefix-based caching and fallback to cached KV to reduce traffic to backends — pushing a config change to edge cache.
Maria G: I'll coordinate with infra to start routing rule change. I want us to keep latency SLO where possible. If draining fails, we'll failover entire host pool for that AZ.
Samir P: Support Pager: start preparing an incident notification for customers noting partial degradation in us-west-2 (single-AZ impact) and SLO mitigation steps. Use status page template.
Support Pager: Draft status posted to #status-drafts: "We are investigating increased errors impacting inference in us-west-2a. Traffic is being shifted while we mitigate. We'll provide updates every 15 minutes."
Liam R: Updates: deregistered 3 targets from target-group tg-inference-usw2a at 14:29 UTC. NLB health checks stabilized for remaining targets.
Jin W: Traffic drop to az1a observed. Error rate down from 6.4% -> 1.1% in the next 90s. Latency still a bit high for a small subset due to sticky sessions.
Maria G: Confirming cross-AZ routing is now handling >95% of inference requests. I'm initiating a canary to bring back small number of requests to az1a after host restart.
Samir P: Did we attempt host restart yet on the noisy nodes?
Liam R: I kicked a rolling restart on the two affected instances (ec2-10-1-3-45 / -46). Reboots started at 14:33 UTC.
ops-bot: aws: EC2 reboot initiated for i-0abc12345 and i-0def67890.
Jin W: Post-reboot we still see kernel driver complaining in dmesg on one node. Suggest we drain it fully and keep it out of rotation until we validate NIC firmware.
Maria G: Agreed — we'll keep it drained. For now, I'll keep routing away from az1a until we validate as healthy for 30m.
Samir P: Customer impact note for postmortem: Customers in us-west-2 experienced elevated 5xx and tail latency for ~12m window (14:23–14:35 UTC). Primary cause: host NIC/ENI packet drops causing NLB target health flaps.
Support Pager: Noted. Sending customer update now.
Jin W: Action items: - collect ENI metrics + dmesg from affected hosts, - open support case with AWS for ENI/driver investigation (include pcap), - review kernel/fw versions on node AMI image.
Liam R: Also: review NLB healthcheck config (intervals, thresholds). consider moving to ALB with HTTP health checks for better app-level detection.
Maria G: I'll run the host forensic collect (logs, `ethtool -S`, `ip -s link`) and drop into S3. Tagging for postmortem.
Samir P: Handoff: Maria will stay on incident lead for next hour; Samir to do follow-up and postmortem. Jin to open AWS support case. Liam to schedule NIC firmware validation on node image. ops-bot will monitor and alert if error rate > 2% in next 30m.
ops-bot: monitor: set threshold 2% on inference-api-prod 30m window.
Maria G: Update 14:49 UTC — error rate stable at ~0.8%, no customer escalations so far. Keeping the AZ out of rotation until 15:10 for verification.
Samir P: Thanks all. We'll create the incident ticket and start a postmortem with timelines + RCA. Closing the active pager but keeping the thread open for follow-ups. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Incident #INC-2026-1991 moved to RESOLVED (mitigated) by Maria G.
Maria G: Post-incident notes to include: consider automating cross-AZ failover earlier, add ENI health hooks in deploy pipeline, and tighten NLB healthcheck to reduce flapping.
Samir P: I'll draft the postmortem and share in #postmortems.
